episodes.title: Ep. 15: Andrew Tate and the Four Controls Every Cult Uses
episodes.description: Kenda came into this one with a stack of research and a question. How does anyone end up in a cult? Her answer starts with Steven Hassan's BITE model, four basic things that all cults have. Behavior, information, thought and emotion. They try to control all of it. She says the people who join are not who you would expect. They are not troubled or unintelligent. They are intelligent people who are searching for connection and something to improve. Kylen brings Andrew Tate. He admits he first took him for a guy who cracked the algorithm and said wild things for clicks. Kenda adds what she found: about 155,000 members in his online university, about 184 million a year, and what UK journalists reported from inside the paid "war rooms". She also watched a Manosphere documentary the night before, and it did not go well for the men on screen. From there they go through the lover boy technique, a Netflix documentary about a TikTok management company that ran like a church and asked for 70 percent of what its members made, a South Korean election that split 58 percent exactly down the line, and the sunk cost fallacy. Then who runs a cult, which is the dark triad, and why 15 percent of men now say they have no close friends. Kylen would like it noted that he is in a cult called Kenda's cult, and she will not let him leave. They end on connection. Everybody wants it, and sometimes the thing we want most is the thing we push away. The Kylen and Kenda Show. Kenda is the mentor. Kylen is the mentee. Sources Kenda names in the episode: Steven Hassan's Combating Cult Mind Control, Pew Research, a Danish report on fake teen accounts, the book Raising Cain, and a Netflix documentary on the 7M TikTok agency. 00:00 Cold open 01:18 Cults, and why we are talking about them 02:14 The BITE model, four things every cult controls 03:01 Who actually joins a cult 05:05 Andrew Tate and the kids who copy him 06:06 Inside a Manosphere documentary 08:58 So what is the Manosphere? 10:33 Labels, semantics and treating people fairly 11:53 Why the Manosphere has a cult element 12:55 "He's just funny": how many people like Andrew Tate 14:21 The Tate war rooms and 184 million a year 16:14 The lover boy technique 18:12 The TikTok cult 19:58 South Korea, and a 58 percent split down the middle 23:31 "It's just true" is where learning stops 24:47 The sunk cost fallacy 26:00 How to be okay with being wrong 27:41 How the Manosphere pulls you in 29:50 Humiliation as entertainment 31:28 How do you join a cult? 32:57 The BITE model as a test 34:08 The cult that took passports 35:21 Who joins and who runs it: the dark triad 37:03 Fear and retaliation 38:27 What school does to a genius preschooler 40:56 The algorithm is the recruiter 42:15 Connection, acceptance and purpose 43:35 Kenda's neighbor 45:19 The loneliness epidemic 45:48 Men, close friends and masculinity influencers 49:15 We push away what we want most 50:12 Everybody craves connection 51:21 Next week: role modeling versus policing
